Prevention: Clean cultivation of mango orchards is the pre-condition of anthracnose disease management.
Ensure adequate light and air by pruning of infected, dead, necrotic and undesirable stems, branches and phanerogamic parasites in the month of
Apply the recommended doses of fertilizer from the last week of

Always harvest and handle fruits carefully to avoid injury.
Harvest mangoes with one inch of stem/petiole.
Post-harvest hot water treatment: put fruits into hot water at 50-55°C for 5-10 minutes (depending on variety).
Cool the fruits by soaking them in tap water for two hours or putting in a well ventilated room.
Monitoring: Regularly (weekly) observe the flowers, fruits, leaves and branches for symptoms.
Look on stems, leaves and flowers for small black spots or black sunken spots.
Monitor more frequently during the flowering stage (a very susceptible stage) and rainy season.
Foggy weather, high temp (25°C), high humidity and rainy conditions all favour disease prevelance and severity.
Observe black spots and tear staining on fruit
Direct Control: Remove rotten fruits from the tree and destroy by burning away from the orchard.
Prune plant parts that show severe symptoms of infection.
Ankuri seed germinator and disinfector for hot water/ vapour treatment to control anthracnose after harvest.
